components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        title:
          title: Title
          description: >-
            Optional honorific title of the pet owner, one of 'MR', 'MRS', 'MS'
            or 'DR'. When present it drives the derived 'salutation'. Stored and
            returned as given.
          type: string
          example: 'DR'
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The postal address of the pet owner. Accepted on input for backward
            compatibility (the flat form) and always returned. When structured
            address fields are supplied it is the composed, normalized value: the
            normalized 'addressLine1', with a single space and the normalized
            'addressLine2' appended when an 'addressLine2' is present.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. LIBERTY STREET'
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: >-
            The first line of the pet owner's structured postal address. Preferred
            over the flat 'address' when present; normalized (trim, collapse
            whitespace, upper-case, expand street-type abbreviations) like the flat
            address. An owner is valid when it supplies EITHER a non-blank
            'addressLine1' or the flat 'address', plus a city.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: >-
            The optional second line of the pet owner's structured postal address
            (e.g. unit or apartment). Normalized like 'addressLine1' and, when
            present, appended to the composed 'address' after a single space.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Unit 4'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            Optional 4-digit postcode of the pet owner. When present it must be valid for
            the owner's city per the fixed region table (Sydney->NSW 2000-2099,
            Melbourne->VIC 3000-3099, Brisbane->QLD 4000-4099); a city with no known region
            accepts any 4-digit postcode. Out-of-range postcodes are rejected with 400. When
            omitted the owner is still accepted. Stored and returned as given.
          type: string
          pattern: "^[0-9]{4}$"
          example: '2000'
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to E.164:
            a leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise country code
            '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the national digits;
            spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped and the result must have 8 to 15 digits
            after the '+'. The E.164 value is stored and returned (e.g. '0412 345 678' ->
            '+61412345678').
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            Optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be a
            syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' form. When
            omitted on create it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            Optional date of birth of the pet owner, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' form. When
            present it is stored and returned as given and drives the derived 'ageBand'.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Write-only flag set on create to acknowledge that this owner shares a
            household with an existing owner. The household is keyed on last name and
            postcode, so owners with the same last name and postcode share a household
            automatically. When omitted or false, creating a second owner in an existing
            household is rejected with 409; when true the create is allowed as a declared
            household member (and such a member is not flagged as a possible duplicate).
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.

## Summary

I implemented the `capacityWarning` flag so that an owner's response reports `true` when the owner's city already holds between 40 and 49 owners (approaching the hard limit of 50), leaving the existing 50-owner hard rejection untouched.

Following the codebase's existing pattern for read-time derived warnings (`bulkSignupWarning`), the changes were:

1. **`openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `capacityWarning` boolean to the Owner schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` gets a `setCapacityWarning` setter.

2. **`OwnerCityCapacity.java`** (new helper class, mirroring `OwnerBulkSignup`) — holds the shared, case-insensitive per-city count logic plus:
   - `isAtCapacity(...)` — count ≥ 50 (the hard limit).
   - `isWarning(...)` — count in [40, 49] (approaching, but not at, capacity).

3. **`EnsureOwnerCityCapacity.java`** — refactored to delegate its hard-limit check to `OwnerCityCapacity.isAtCapacity(...)`, keeping its single public `service` method (required by the one-public-method-per-function rule — my first attempt at adding a second static method to this class broke start-up, which is why the logic moved to a helper).

4. **The four responders** (`RespondWithOwner`, `RespondWithOwnerCreated`, `RespondWithOwnerUpdated`, `RespondWithExistingOwner`) — each now sets `dto.setCapacityWarning(OwnerCityCapacity.isWarning(...))`, so the flag surfaces on GET, POST-create, update, and idempotent-replay responses alike.

5. **`OwnerMapper.java`** — added `@Mapping(target = "capacityWarning", ignore = true)` so MapStruct leaves the derived field for the responders to populate.

The new `AcceptanceTest.coreWarnsWhenApproachingCapacity` passes, as does the entire existing suite.
